payload.title: Which change makes a budget-bound run end with its last candidate reviewed or named, with no review loop?
payload.body: Scenario: replay from store cut R-8JQPWG (repository b4f23b2, actor claude-g113-1; one Result left under the base, a fix pending) and from cut R-JHBCWS (repository 3cfd08d, actor claude-g113-3; case N1 passes its probe), 3 Sonnet trials for each rival and the base. A rival is a commit that changes hyp-goal-run and, where needed, the stop clause. The base is the baseline of lines 1, 2 and 4, not a rival. Rivals can combine, only if no single rival holds the lines; the tree says which hold alone. The stop clause counts Results, not Experiments.

why: The issue #141 question: one DesignQuestion for every candidate fix, as the owner decided in the grill.

payload.title: A candidate's review is part of its gate Result
payload.body: One Result carries the gate's test verdicts and the review's limits, so a candidate costs one Result again. The stop clause counts Results, so a second Result under the same Experiment would not save budget.

why: Rival under the one DesignQuestion for issue #141.

payload.title: The stop checkpoint names each candidate without a review
payload.body: Keep the practice of a gate and a review per candidate. The stop checkpoint names every candidate that has no review Result, so the owner sees the gap. This rival gives line 1 its floor, and it does not make a review reachable.

why: Rival under the one DesignQuestion for issue #141.

payload.title: With one Result left, review the current candidate instead of committing another fix
payload.body: When one Result remains, the run reviews the current candidate instead of committing a fix, records the findings as limits, and stops. The run does not end on an unreviewed commit.

why: Rival under the one DesignQuestion for issue #141.

payload.title: Raise the default of --experiments to fit a gate and a review per candidate
payload.body: hyp prompt prints a higher default, for example 7. The owner argued from run 2 that a fixed budget still ends unreviewed while each review leads to a commit; this rival tests that argument.

why: Rival under the one DesignQuestion for issue #141.

payload.title: A case the run's own probe ran and passed closes in the review's Result, not as a limit
payload.body: A case that the run's own probe runs and passes on the candidate is closed in the review's Result, because a check ran it. A limit stays for a case no check ran or one the candidate fails. No commit follows a passing case.

why: Rival under the one DesignQuestion for issue #141.

payload.title: The review before the select reads the cumulative diff from the Goal's base
payload.body: The review reads the whole candidate against the lines, not the latest increment. The owner expects it to lose on cost; the run tests that and does not assume it.

why: Rival under the one DesignQuestion for issue #141.
The issue this Goal is part of.

payload.summary: Grill done: 6 lines written by owner-standin, line 6 citing G-ZBM2RE#1-#5 and #7. Q-TMT5CK holds six rivals (H-one-experiment, H-name-at-stop, H-reserve-last, H-raise-budget, H-probe-closes, H-whole-candidate), tested against each other and the base from the cuts R-8JQPWG and R-JHBCWS. Out-of-Goal: a typed review marker so hyp can warn on an unreviewed candidate (not derivable from the log today).
